projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: High device connectivity (24–26) paired with zero motion or camera activity for four hours suggests the household is likely gathered in a single, non-monitored space (e.g., home theater or basement) or has disabled motion tracking, but the complete lack of physical activity warrants a quick wellness check to rule out sensor blind spots or unresponsiveness.

The sustained presence of 20–25 devices combined with zero camera or motion activity for four hours strongly indicates a presence detection anomaly (likely neighbor device bleed or cached connections) rather than actual occupancy, as a household with children and active dogs would typically trigger motion sensors on a Saturday evening.

The sustained presence of 19–25 mobile devices combined with zero camera/motion activity for four hours on a Saturday evening strongly indicates a large, settled gathering (likely extended family or friends) occupying a common area, with additional guests connecting around 7:14 PM. This explains the lack of typical household activity and suggests elevated network load or security monitoring may be warranted.

The stable presence of ~20 devices combined with zero motion/camera activity strongly suggests the household is gathered in a single sensor-blind zone (e.g., media room or basement) or that motion sensors are offline. This creates a monitoring gap during peak occupancy, so verifying sensor status or adjusting automation triggers for this area is recommended.

The sustained presence of 20–25 devices paired with zero camera/motion activity for four hours on a Saturday afternoon strongly suggests the family is engaged in a prolonged stationary activity (e.g., movie marathon, gaming, or napping) or has motion detection disabled; the stabilization at 20 devices at 16:55 confirms a settled, low-activity state rather than an absence.

The stable 24–29 connected devices paired with zero motion/camera activity for four hours indicates the household is likely gathered in a single zone engaged in a stationary activity, confirming everyone is home and settled rather than dispersed; this is typical for a relaxed Saturday but suggests motion sensors may be less sensitive or obstructed in that specific area.

The sustained 19-22 device count paired with zero motion/camera activity on a Saturday afternoon strongly indicates a stationary gathering (e.g., guests or a kids' playdate) with devices charging or in use in camera blind spots, which aligns with normal weekend household patterns rather than a system anomaly.

The sustained high device count (19-22) combined with zero motion and camera activity for four hours strongly suggests a presence system false positive or that all devices are stationary in a non-monitored zone, indicating the home may actually be unoccupied despite network reports.

The sustained count of 19-24 connected devices alongside zero camera or motion activity for four hours strongly suggests a network or IoT device counting anomaly rather than actual occupancy, especially given the small household size.

The presence system reports 19-23 connected devices despite zero camera or motion activity and a recent drop to 19, strongly indicating the household has left the house while the network still registers their devices or IoT gadgets as present. This mismatch could cause automated systems to incorrectly assume occupancy, so verify departure status and consider resetting presence tracking.
